28860.explanation: The upper chamber, often known as the upper house or the Senate, serves as a revising and reviewing body. 28861.explanation: In the case of the Soviet Union, the constituent republics had the theoretical right to secede from the union according to the 1924 Soviet Constitution, although this was not practically allowed by the central government. 28917.subject: Government
28917.question_text: Which constitution was created to legislate for the Lagos Colony and the Southern Provinces?
28917.explanation: The Clifford Constitution (1922) was introduced in colonial Nigeria to provide limited legislative representation for the Lagos Colony and the Southern Provinces. It aimed to increase African participation in government but was criticised for favouring the South over the North. This constitution preceded the Richards Constitution (1946) and the Macpherson Constitution (1951), and it focused on Southern Nigeria specifically, unlike later constitutions which included the North more fully.

28935.subject: Government
28935.question_text: Who was appointed by the federal government of Nigeria as the administrator of Western Region in 1962?
28935.explanation:
Dr MA Majekodunmi was elected into the Nigerian Senate in 1960. He was appointed sole administrator of Western Region in June 1962 after a political crisis in the region, holding office in place of the Premier Samuel Akintola until December that year.[7]

The crisis was due to a struggle between Akintola and the former Western Region Premier and current leader of the opposition Obafemi Awolowo, which had led to violent scenes in the House of Assembly. On advice from the police, one of his first acts was to sign restriction orders to detain leaders of both factions.[7] After the situation had stabilized, Akintola resumed office on 1 January 1963.[8]

28953.question_text: Which of these groups of Africa leaders in closely associated with the formation of the OAU
28953.explanation:
The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was established on 25 May 1963 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Its formation was championed by key African leaders who were committed to African unity, independence and cooperation.

The prominent leaders associated with the OAU’s formation include:

  • Kwame Nkrumah (Ghana) – strong advocate of Pan-Africanism
  • Julius Nyerere (Tanzania) – supported unity and anti-colonialism
  • Haile Selassie (Ethiopia) – hosted the founding conference
